battlecards.why_selected: Provided lowest total landed cost through HPG tier, committed to 12-month firm pricing and supported full consolidation of SKUs across 30+ clinics.
battlecards.contract_terms: Master distribution agreement executed 30-Jul-2021; 12-month firm pricing (excluding Rx) then mutual renegotiation for additional 12 months; primary GPO-linked formularies.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive RFP with four national distributors plus dual-GPO benchmarks created pricing pressure; APDerm willingness to shift 100 % volume.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: National scale, deep dermatology formulary, next-day delivery to New England region.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial invoices showed price discrepancies requiring post-award audit.
battlecards.switching_costs: Clinic staff retraining on McKesson ordering portal, back-end item cross-referencing.

battlecards.why_selected: Offered most competitive pricing on scheduled routes and could flex capacity for STAT medical specimens.
battlecards.contract_terms: Ground Transportation Agreement amendment effective Aug-2021; initial 3-year term with fixed stop & mileage rates; 30-day termination for cause.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Bundled 33-location network into fewer optimised routes; threat of awarding full book to competitor.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Established healthcare courier, HIPAA-trained drivers, real-time tracking.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Smaller geographic reach outside New England compared with nationals.
battlecards.switching_costs: Route re-mapping and specimen pickup time changes at clinics.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided best value on on-demand STAT work and weekend coverage, complementing Millers scheduled routes.
battlecards.contract_terms: Service agreement drafted Aug-2021, 3-year term, fuel surcharge cap 8 %, quarterly KPI review.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to split business between two carriers kept pricing aggressive.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: 24/7 control tower, women-owned (WBENC), extensive medical reference base.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher minimum stop charge than Millers on some rural routes.
battlecards.switching_costs: Labeling changes for specimen bags, system interface for pickup requests.

battlecards.why_selected: Bundled circuits with managed services, offered 38 % TCO reduction and single invoice for all sites.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year MSA with optional 1-year renewals; flat MRCs, no early termination fees on newly groomed circuits.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat to disconnect redundant circuits; competitive quotes from cable MSOs; commitment to add new sites.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Proactive monitoring, SD-WAN roadmap, ability to leverage Verizon wholesale rates.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Implementation lead time 60-90 days for fiber upgrades.
battlecards.switching_costs: CPE replacement, porting of static IPs.

battlecards.why_selected: Met lowest total cost on standard laptop and desktop bundles and agreed to hold pricing for 12 months.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing MOU (Sep-2021) covering core SKU list; same-day quote turnaround SLA; 30-day net terms.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Standardised on two device configurations, enabling direct cross-bid comparison; year-on-year growth forecast shared.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong Lenovo & Dell relationships, imaging services included, rapid order fulfillment.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited e-commerce portal functionality versus Connection.
battlecards.switching_costs: Update golden image, reroute warranty claims.

battlecards.why_selected: Matched Alves’ blended rate within incumbent framework and agreed to 10 % reduction in hours within 3 months.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year agreement effective 1-Jun-2022; hourly rate $26.60 locked year 1; hours reduced 10 % by Sept-2022; Net 30; discounted rates for new acquisitions.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Lower-priced BAFO from Alves created credible switch threat; volume across 33 sites.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing footprint, dedicated onsite supervisors, mobile time-tracking app.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher hourly rate than challenger prior to BAFO, inconsistent staffing at smaller sites.
battlecards.switching_costs: Training new crews, key card issuance, infection-control SOP transfer.
battlecards.notes: Scenario analysis showed full switch to Alves could have saved $312 K but raised coverage concerns at 6 sites.

battlecards.why_selected: Maintained functionality while offering 0.30 % reduction in revenue-share and 3-year rate lock.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year rate lock; tiered rates—1.50 % up to $150 M, 1.45 % next $100 M, 1.40 % above; quarterly look-back; cosmetics carved-out.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Issued multi-vendor RFP and demonstrated willingness to migrate; projected revenue growth to $250 M enhanced volume argument.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Mature collector platform, integration with existing EHR, minimal transition risk.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher statement fees vs competitors, limited flexibility on ancillary modules.
battlecards.switching_costs: Provider re-credentialing, data migration risk, downtime on claims submissions.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided lower CPC rates and included software for remote meter reads; aligned with GPO contract.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed 60-month FMV lease; black CPC $0.0065, color $0.045; installation of KM Consult App for automated reporting.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Pulled actual meter data to challenge incumbent volumes; GPO rate benchmarks.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: National service network, advanced fleet monitoring, unified billing.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Long lease tenor commits APDerm for 5 years.
battlecards.switching_costs: Device swap-out and staff training on new UI.

battlecards.why_selected: Premier GPO markup (62 %) beat incumbent average 82 % and included direct-hire conversion terms.
battlecards.contract_terms: Premier GPO agreement; 62 % markup on regular time, 50 % OT premium; no conversion fee after 520 hours.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated volume + GPO pre-negotiated ceiling rates.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Large clinical talent pool, on-line timesheet portal, nationwide reach.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Less local office presence in some rural MA markets.
battlecards.switching_costs: Onboarding new agency portal; background check credentials.

battlecards.why_selected: Treya GPO program provided superior discounts and dimensional weight relief.
battlecards.contract_terms: Treya Group Purchasing Member Agreement signed Apr-2021; discounts off UPS Daily Rates plus 166 DIM factor; evergreen with 30-day exit.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: FedEx historical data used to model target discounts; GPO scale.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Ground network reliability, healthcare compliance, daily pick-up included.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Fuel surcharge volatility; limited Saturday ground pick-up in some areas.
battlecards.switching_costs: Labeling software swap, staff training on WorldShip.

battlecards.why_selected: Matched benchmark pricing on top 150 SKUs and introduced 3 % annual rebate, avoiding change management effort.
battlecards.contract_terms: Updated price file effective Jun-2021; 1-year price hold on core list; 3 % rebate on spend $50–100 K, quarterly check.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Presented alternative marketplace pricing and threatened pilot with Amazon Business.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Next-day delivery, furniture assembly services, consolidated invoices.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher pricing volatility on non-core items, fuel surcharge added in 2022.
battlecards.switching_costs: None significant—but user familiarity and order templates favor incumbent.

summary.skipped_reason: Suppliers in categories with minor renewals (e.g., Telecom PBX, Uniforms) or insufficient strategic data were omitted.

extraction_notes: Savings, baseline and lever details sourced from Phase 1 & Phase 2 Final Close-out report dated 5-Aug-2022.
Contract terms pulled from specific contract drafts (UPS Member Agreement, Janitorial MOU, Courier amendments, etc.).
Where final spend by individual courier was not isolated, category-level savings applied; final spend set null.
